PC: Ask patient and/or patient’s mother about subjective symptoms consistent with influenza, including cough, shortness of breath, fever, myalgias. Students should also complete a review of systems
Auscultate the patient’s lungs and identify bilateral crackles
MK: Recognize that a patient with a new fever on a hospital floor with a known influenza outbreak is likely to have influenza
SBP: Understand that influenza is spread by droplets and fomites, and therefore requires both droplet and contact precautions – don gown, gloves, and surgical mask.
Students should place diagnostic orders (influenza PCR) and infection control orders (contact and droplet precautions); facilitators can prompt if not already done.
Students should remove gowns, gloves, and masks and perform hand hygiene.
ICS: Explain to the patient and her mother that they will be testing for influenza (and possibly other respiratory viruses.)
